reply_text:
㊥ (*Warnings* popping up) The warnings popping up now aren't from the 象 recorder. Both of your last turns were recorded through the JVM cleanly (`turn-elJzmq` is analysed; this one, `turn-PhLBYe`, is waiting for my reply to end). The three "NOT recorded" lines are left over from before the parser fix. The new warnings come from `server-dead-client.el`: "20 emacsclient replies dropped in the last 5 min". It warns when Emacs answers emacsclient calls too slowly and the callers give up.

🈖 (what that warning means) Agency runs emacsclient calls against your Emacs, for example the blackboard projections, and kills them if they're slow. The file's own note says the cause on 2026-10-03 was "six forgotten tty frames redrawing busy REPL buffers". The counter is at 1,183 drops in total, with 5 in the current 5-minute window, so it's quieter at the moment. It warns at most once every 10 minutes.

㊬ (not the recorder) I timed the JVM turn route at about 1 ms per request. Recording at send is synchronous, but it doesn't stall Emacs. The polls for readings are asynchronous.

㊟ (frames) Your Emacs has four tty frames besides the initial one:
- **F16** on `/dev/pts/2`: this buffer
- **F13** on `/dev/pts/24`: `*codex-repl:codex-19*`
- **F12** on `/dev/pts/21`: `*codex-repl:codex-10*`
- **F14** on `/dev/pts/21`: a corfu completion popup

Each visible REPL buffer redraws as it streams, and that's what the earlier incident traced the slowness to.

🈸 (one decision) Is F12 (codex-10, on pts/21) a frame you still use? If not, closing it with `C-x 5 0` in that terminal should cut the redraw load. I can delete it from here if you prefer. Separately, I could make the warning log to `*Messages*` instead of popping up `*Warnings*`, if you'd rather it didn't interrupt.

🈯 (slicing the inference) On the different ways to slice the inference: rather than picking one now, 象 could produce more than one reading of the same pair, and we see which ones prove useful. That fits the M-象-cascade view that multiplicity "is information too". I'll put it in the lab note if you want that written.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what went wrong) Two separate problems:
- **The timeout.** The JVM wrote the record at 23:57:56, then ran the 小象 draft inside the same request until 23:58:07. Emacs warned "Turn structure was NOT recorded … no answer" and never stored the record's path.
- **The wrong turn.** Your buffer was still pointing at the previous turn's record (`turn-SuuilW`, already read). Without correcting that, the end of this reply would have reported "happened" for the wrong turn.
